hypothesis: Cacheable EL1 table walks with a per-core flush, a per-boot table checksum and one table builder fit the instruction, maintenance and table-write budgets in instruction models.
prediction: Budgets (baseline -> budget, measured by). Table writes after the builder returns: 16 statements (counted) -> 0 (capacity check writer scan). EL1 TCR value repeated outside the header and its reader: 16 files (counted) -> 0 (source scan in checks/cpu-table-walks.py). Flush before the first table write in a733_cached_memory_prepare(): not checked -> flush call precedes the builder call (disassembly scan). enable_el1 instructions, success path: 75 (counted) -> at most 2,500 (coherence check emulation). Table-line maintenance per boot, cached eight-core image: 320 DC CVAC (counted) -> 320 DC CIVAC at EL3 plus 128 per core, 1,344, and 1,664 until the continue.c publication is dropped (coherence check DC trace). Cached single-core image: 0 -> 448. Table readback per core and boot: 0 -> 512 LDP (1,024 words). DRAM mapped at EL1; table memory: 910 MiB; 20 KiB -> 910 MiB until stage 2, then 2,958 MiB; 20 KiB plus 64 B (capacity check golden map). Descriptor reads served by DRAM per EL1 walk: every read that misses the walk caches (non-cacheable) -> only reads that miss the data caches (board). Added boot work is about 1,000 cache-maintenance operations, an estimated 0.15 ms at 494 MHz if each costs at most 70 cycles, and 512 uncached loads per core, an estimated 0.1 ms at 200 ns each; both run once per boot. QEMU does not model caches or walk latency. Reasoning: A733_CPU_COHERENCE_TCR (0x200803019) makes the EL1 table walker read descriptors as Normal non-cacheable memory (IRGN0 = ORGN0 = 0b00), so every descriptor read that misses the walk caches goes to DRAM; setting IRGN0 = ORGN0 = 0b01 (write-back, read-allocate, write-allocate) gives 0x200803519, the value platform_init() in platform/a733/platform.c already uses. A cacheable walker can hit a stale cache line over a table page, hence the flush before the first descriptor write (DC CIVAC at EL3 over the five pages removes any Secure dirty line that could be evicted over a descriptor; the former DC CVAC publication after the writes would write such a line back over the new descriptors), the per-core DC CIVAC over the EL1 root and level-2 pages at EL1 entry (EL1 with the MMU off addresses the Non-secure space, which is the alias the EL1 walker reads), and the checksum check. Eight-core images keep 0x200803019 because no Cortex-A76 walk-cost source is pinned; with non-cacheable walks the flush removes a stale line that a later eviction could write over the tables and the check refuses tables such a write-back corrupted.

conclusion: Every budget is met except two, both by one line from the same cause: the EL3 flush covers the whole table section including the 64-byte checksum line, 321 lines instead of 320, so the eight-core count is 321 at EL3 plus 128 per core on eight cores (1,345; 1,666 while the continue.c publication remains, which has since been dropped) and the single-core count is 321 plus 128 = 449. The prepared table pages differ from base in two words only: level-1 entry 0 of the EL3 and EL1 regimes gains SH = 0b10. The checksum is a 64-byte array so its line holds nothing else; Clang emits the section's objects in the order memory.c first names them and memory.c names the checksum last; checks/cpu-table-walks.py verifies it follows the five pages in each image. TCR_EL1 installed by the eight-core entry is 0x200803019; the single-core value's low half is loaded before every TCR_EL1 write. Each added instruction and barrier runs once per boot or once per core entry; no metric changes on a path that runs after the scheduler starts. Coherence check passes 41 cases; the reservation check and eight-core scheduler model pass; the capacity check passes its four modes on eight QEMU CPUs with 392 translations and 22,547 preparation instructions, the same counts as before.
narrative: Results (metric: base / budget / head). Table writes after the builder returns (writer-scan hits): 17 (16 statements and one patch context line in apps/dsi-scanout/monitor.patch and apps/storage-read-single-core/monitor.c) / 0 / 0. Files that spell the EL1 TCR value outside the header and frozen images: base literal scan 22 files, 11 remain at head (the header, which now holds both values, and ten files for the non-cacheable continuation profile and the frozen production image); the eleven removed are the two assembly sources, eight single-core and coherence host checks, and checks/storage-read-single-core.py; the design counted ten, omitting that last check. Flush before the first table write: none / precedes the builder / precedes the builder and every table-section write. enable_el1 instructions 75 / at most 2,500 / 2,233. Table-line maintenance eight-core 320 DC CVAC / 1,344 or 1,664 / 1,345 or 1,666; single-core 0 / 448 / 449. Table readback 0 / 512 LDP / 512 LDP. Table memory 20,480 B / 20,544 B / 20,544 B. EL1 mapping 126 MiB of Normal DRAM in the diagnostic image at base and head (the capacity check's 910 MiB figure applies to the extended device-memory profile, which this image does not enable). Other costs (base / head): a733_cached_memory_prepare() instructions, eight-core 11,669 / 15,596 (the 321-line flush and the checksum over two pages), single-core 11,702 / 15,629; barriers in a733_cached_memory_prepare() 0 / 1 DSB SY; DSB and ISB in enable_el1 success path 11 / 15; single-core table check check_el1 absent / 2,189 instructions, 512 LDP, 128 DC CIVAC, no system-register write; table-section writes during preparation 2,694 / 2,695 (the checksum word); .text eight-core 51,200 B / 53,248 B; changed functions eight-core +1,216 B (flush 208 B and check_el1 500 B new, enable_el1 +376 B, a733_cached_memory_prepare() +132 B); .text single-core 492,224 B / 492,224 B (platform_init() grows by 56 B inside existing alignment padding). Implementation notes: the flush loop handles four lines and the readback loop one line per pass to stay within the instruction budget; only whole table pages get the EL3 Normal non-cacheable mapping, the partial page holding the checksum keeps the Device mapping, leaving the EL3 map unchanged; the EL1 table check and enable sit in their own input section .text.a733_cpu_coherence_el1 with their own refusal exit, because both read a733_cached_el1_table_sum, which only the cached table builder defines, so an image that links cpu_coherence.S for publication alone (the microSD single-core image) drops them under --gc-sections (a program that calls only a733_cpu_coherence_publish() fails with an undefined a733_cached_el1_table_sum when both functions share the main section; the microSD single-core image did not build at that time for an unrelated reason, five objects of its USB2 host library not compiling (hcd.h missing, TUSB_SPEED_SUPER undeclared), and its link command on the other 161 objects reported only the eight USB2 host symbols as undefined, plus a733_cached_el1_table_sum with an object keeping both functions in the main section); a733_cached_memory_prepare() takes no deadline argument so its flush uses a 10 ms bound from its own counter read, and the single-core platform_init() also passes 10 ms. checks/cpu-table-walks.py holds only the cases that need a linked image: the TCR literal scan and header values, the flush before the builder and before the first table write, the checksum layout and the checksum as the last table write, the success-path counts, the writer scan, the eight-core TCR_EL1 value and, in each single-core image, the table check and the cached value before the TCR_EL1 write. Primitive cases live in checks/a733-cpu-coherence.py: a corrupted checksum and a root entry 1 outside the monitor interval, naming the root itself or carrying attribute bits leave SCTLR_EL1.M clear and write no system register; check_el1 writes no system register on success or refusal; the flush primitive cleans every line of a partial range at EL3 and EL1 and refuses with no DC a range below or beyond DRAM, an empty range, EL2, unmasked DAIF, SCTLR.C set at EL3 or EL1, and an expired deadline. Layout of the change: EL1 TCR value taken from include/a733_cpu_coherence.h by assembly (C declarations under #ifndef __ASSEMBLER__) and by Python through tools/a733_tcr.py, which parses the header and refuses any other selection of A733_CPU_COHERENCE_TCR; literal sites that stay: the non-cacheable continuation profile in platform/a733/cpu_continue.{S,c} and checks/a733-cpu-continue.py (MAIR = 0x4400, all RAM non-cacheable), the frozen apps/gpu-finite/return-check.py, every TCR_EL3 literal, and the native startup and cache probes (boot/a733/native-el1-cache-probe.S, checks/native-startup-probe.py, tools/run-native-startup-probe.py, tools/prepare-primary-cache-probe.py, tools/secondary-cache-host.py, tools/all-core-pre-scheduler-host.py), which enter EL1 through a production eight-core image pinned by SHA-256 whose a733_cached_enter_el1 sets 0x200803019. continue.S changes are the TCR triple (same length, same value in eight-core images), an include of a733_cpu_coherence.h on line 2 and the removal of one of two consecutive blank lines before line 273; the observe hook (platform/a733-smp-observe/continue.patch, also applied by the supervised build) adds an SVC 120 dispatch at line 336 and the storage hooks (platform/a733-storage-maintenance/continue.patch) change the fatal path at line 273 and the EL1t vectors at line 307; no hook reads TCR or the tables and every hunk applies with --fuzz=0 at the same offset as before. Level-1 entry 0 (the MMIO block) gains SH = 0b10 in both regimes, removing the 16 later writes in apps/storage-read-single-core/monitor.c (seven image branches) and apps/dsi-scanout/monitor.patch (one branch); core 0 stores a 64-bit additive checksum of the two EL1 pages in a733_cached_el1_table_sum, a 64-byte-aligned word in .bss.a733_cached_tables. a733_cpu_coherence_flush(base, bytes, deadline) requires EL3 or EL1 with the MMU and data cache off, masked exceptions, 64-byte data lines and a range inside 0x40000000-0x48000000; DC CIVAC never discards data so a deadline refusal leaves memory unchanged. platform_init() flushes level1 and level2 with a 10 ms deadline each before the first write and again after the last, before msr ttbr0_el1. Synchronization: no lock is needed because the tables are immutable after preparation and the record barrier in continue.c holds secondaries; for a stale line in another core's cache to be removed, DC CIVAC issued with the MMU off must reach every cache in the Outer Shareable domain, which the Arm Architecture Reference Manual states for Device-type accesses but is not pinned. Device shareability: TF-A 0892ad4 xlat_tables_core.c treats Device memory as Outer Shareable regardless of SH, so the moved SH = 0b10 changes no behaviour. TCR walk attributes: TF-A 0892ad4 lib/xlat_tables_v2/aarch64/xlat_tables_arch.c setup_mmu_cfg() sets TCR_RGN_INNER_WBA | TCR_RGN_OUTER_WBA with Inner Shareable walks whenever its tables are cacheable (archive hash in docs/cpu-coherence.md). Cortex-A55 TRM 100442_0200_00 (SHA-256 1f71b74d...7dd97) sections A5.5.1 (walks are cacheable only with write-back IRGN and ORGN and the cache enabled), A5.2.2, A6.2.4 and C2.4. Unproven and unpinned: the Cortex-A76 equivalents of those TRM sections; the Arm Architecture Reference Manual rules that EL3 with the MMU off addresses the Secure space, that EL1 with the MMU off addresses the Non-secure space, and that maintenance issued with the MMU off reaches every core; whether the A733 has a system cache beyond the DSU. Left out: cacheable EL3 walks (EL3 walks only at boot and on faults and its tables must stay non-cacheable for its data accesses); one flush on core 0 instead of one per core (saves 896 operations per boot but needs the EL1 entry order in continue.c to change); the contiguous hint on dma32 blocks (the 2 MiB blocks already fit the level-2 TLB; it returns if an A/B run shows DTLB_WALK costing more than 1% of CPU_CYCLES in a workload); moving the single-core platform_init() onto enable_el1 (it would change the sequence that seven emulator checks model); stage-3 entries 4 to 12 (they need launch evidence for 0x1_0000_0000-0x3_4000_0000).

hypothesis: Cacheable EL1 walks (TCR_EL1 0x200803519) use no more cycles per forced walk than non-cacheable walks (0x200803019) on Cortex-A55 core 0.
prediction: Revert rule: image B (cached walks) must not use more cycles than image A (uncached) beyond the spread of five runs; otherwise A733_CPU_COHERENCE_TCR_CACHED_WALK reverts to the uncached value. Estimate: 50 to 75 cycles per DRAM descriptor read at 494 MHz against 30 to 50 cycles for an L3 hit. Steady-state walks should be rare, because the A55's 1,024-entry level-2 TLB holds 2 MiB blocks (TRM section A5.2.2) and the EL1 map needs fewer than 470 entries. The forced-walk loop is TLBI VMALLE1, DSB, ISB and one load from a different 2 MiB block per iteration, recording CPU_CYCLES (event 0x11) and DTLB_WALK (0x34) on core 0.

hypothesis: No Non-secure dirty line covers an EL1 table page when a core enters EL1, so the entry flush never writes a stale line over the descriptors.
prediction: On the Cortex-A55, DC IVAC cleans a dirty line before invalidating it (TRM 100442_0200_00 section A6.2.4) and DC CIVAC always does. If a Non-secure dirty line covers an EL1 table page at entry, the EL1 entry flush writes it back over the descriptors and the table check then stops the core before any translation register is written. docs/cold-entry.md specifies the experiment for each launch path: EL3, with the MMU off, fills the five pages with a known pattern, cleans them with DC CVAC through the Non-secure alias using the temporary mapping of platform/a733-smp-supervised/publication.S, then reads them back through the Secure alias and records every changed word. It passes when no word changes in three cold boots per path. A failure moves the Non-secure flush before the first write, which needs an EL3 mapping of the Non-secure alias during the build. It is the first run of the first board session that uses these images.
narrative: Open board run listed under the open work of docs/designs/cpu-table-walks.md.
